name: title

split.note: A title whose lede overflows the page (measured, so only a title that does not fit) keeps its eyebrow and title on the cover and gives its lede paragraphs a page of their own after it, on the same canvas (owner, 2026-11-15; fit-everywhere-model.md §25). A title that fits never splits. lib/core/carousel.js title-lede.

description: Opening slide. Dark canvas, centered, no chrome.
purpose: First slide of every deck. Sets the topic and the visual tone. Drops the running header and the page number, and keeps the deck's footer, its standing note (a "Confidential" or a copyright), by the anchor-chrome rule (engineering/decisions/2026-11-08-anchor-chrome.md). `silent` drops every band in one token. On a phone, a title whose lede runs past the page splits: the cover keeps the eyebrow, the title and the deck's footer, and the lede (with anything authored after it) takes one page of its own on the same canvas; a lede longer than that page still clips, and the export says so. A title that fits never splits (engineering/decisions/2026-10-28-fit-everywhere-model.md §25). Add `spectrum` when the deck itself is built on a multi-step color story (a level system, a spectrum of stages) worth echoing here. The deck's `cover: light` register repaints the front and back cover together on the deck's light canvas, in both color modes (`cover-light`; a slide opts out with `cover-inverse`). `light` alone sets a scheme and keeps the dark panel (lib/base/base.registers.docs.md § cover). Seven cover compositions (`cover-masthead`, `cover-ledger`, `cover-column`, `cover-label`, `cover-stage`, `cover-frame`, `cover-poster`) set how the heading block sits; the deck writes one with the same register's second word (`cover: light column`) so both covers match, and `cover-plain` keeps one slide centered. A `cover-stage` or `cover-poster` heading holds about 60 characters; a longer one grows down from the top of the frame and overflows at the foot.

heading.description:
Deck title. Capped at `--measure-bookend-heading` (16em ≈ 33 characters) so a long title composes as a block rather than a full-width banner; `text-wrap: balance` evens the lines. Override the token in front-matter `style:` — never hand-break with `
`.

eyebrow.description: Optional category label rendered above the h1 (authored as an inline-code paragraph immediately after the h1; flex `order` lifts it above).

subtitle.description: Optional plain-paragraph subtitle below the h1. Uncapped — title's subtitle is a single tagline, unlike closing's, which takes `--measure-bookend-lede`.

whenToUse.title: First slide of every deck
whenToUse.body: Sets topic, audience, and visual tone in one glance. The dark canvas anchors the deck visually so subsequent slides feel like a continuous document.

whenToUse.title: Brand or section bookends
whenToUse.body: Pair with `divider` (mid-deck section breaks) and `closing` (the final slide) for the full anchor trio. All three share the dark-bookend treatment.

whenToUse.title: Pitch and proposal openings
whenToUse.body: When the audience needs the headline and the framing line before any data. The subtitle paragraph is where the framing line goes.

antiPatterns.title: Mid-deck statements
antiPatterns.body: Use `big-number` or `content` for emphatic statements inside a deck. Reaching for the title chrome mid-deck breaks the bookend signal.

antiPatterns.title: Multi-line h1
antiPatterns.body: Keep the h1 to one editorial line. The layout is centered and large — two-line titles get cramped and lose impact.

antiPatterns.title: Header or footer overrides
antiPatterns.body: Don't blank the footer with `_footer: ''` on a title slide. The footer is the deck's standing note (a "Confidential", a copyright), and a cover is where a reader most expects it. Drop it on purpose with `no-footer`, or every band with `silent`.

related.name: divider
related.when: mid-deck section breaks — same dark-bookend chrome

related.name: closing
related.when: the final slide — closes the bookend pair

commonMistakes.mistake: Eyebrow written as bold or plain text instead of inline code, e.g. `**Category · Date**`.
commonMistakes.fix: Wrap the eyebrow paragraph in backticks. The eyebrow CSS matches `h1 + p:has(> code:only-child)`; without the code span the paragraph falls through to the general subtitle rule instead — it still renders styled, just as a second subtitle line, not the eyebrow lifted above the h1.

commonMistakes.mistake: The subtitle paragraph is authored before the eyebrow paragraph instead of after it.
commonMistakes.fix: The eyebrow match is an immediate-next-ELEMENT-sibling selector (`h1 + p:has(> code:only-child)`) — it only counts element siblings, so an HTML comment between the h1 and the eyebrow is harmless, but another paragraph is not. Keep the source order heading → eyebrow → subtitle.

commonMistakes.mistake: Inline emphasis (`**bold**`, `_italic_`) inside the h1 itself.
commonMistakes.fix: Keep the h1 to plain text. The centered, oversized type already carries full weight — nested emphasis at that scale reads as noise, not emphasis.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to author the spectrum bar as a markdown `---`/`***` rule instead of the `spectrum` class.
commonMistakes.fix: Every top-level `hr` token in a slide body is the slide separator (it splits the deck into a new slide) — there is no way to hand-author a literal rule element here. Add the `spectrum` class instead; the bar is CSS-generated.
